title: Site-wide Degradation and Database Saturation via Auth Retry Storm
triggerEvent: Deployment of auth-service v2.4.1 introducing a synchronous regex-based JWT token validation step.
summary: A deployment to the auth-service introduced a CPU-intensive regex operation, causing latency spikes. This triggered a retry storm from the API Gateway, which overwhelmed the auth-service. The auth-service subsequently saturated the Redis Cache and Primary Database connection pools, leading to a complete failure of the checkout flow and other dependent services.

timeline.event: Monitoring: All systems healthy. Baseline telemetry nominal.
Deployment: auth-service v2.4.1 rolled out to production (Deploy #882).
Weak Signal: Slight auth-service latency increase (P99 from 25ms to 100ms) detected.
Warning: auth-service P99 latency crosses 250ms threshold. Automated alert fired.
False Alarm: Engineer dismisses latency warning as expected morning traffic burst.
Temporary Stabilization: auth-service latency returns to 50ms. Gateway traffic appears stable.
Warning Returns: Massive traffic spike hits auth-service. Latency violently spikes > 400ms.
Service Degradation: auth-service CPU pegs at 100%. gateway-service begins experiencing 504 timeouts.
Dependency Impact: gateway-service retry storm overwhelms redis-cache thread pool. checkout-service latency spikes to 4500ms.
Dependency Impact: primary-db connection pool exhausted by auth-service fallbacks. payments-service and inventory-service failing.
Incident Declaration: Global Error Rate > 20%. PagerDuty triggers SEV-1. War room assembled.
RCA: IncidentMind Core begins causality parsing. Engine analyzing logs and commits.
Recovery Recommendation: System identifies regex commit and recommends rollback to v2.4.0.
Operator Action: Operator explicitly approves rollback recommendation.
Recovery: auth-service v2.4.0 pods active. Latency drops back to 25ms.
Recovery Confirmed: primary-db connections drop to 20%. redis-cache CPU stabilized. Checkout flow operational.
Monitoring: Continuous polling confirms no further errors across infrastructure.

failurePropagation.reason: Increased processing time in auth-service breached API Gateway timeouts, causing 504 errors.
API Gateway's automated retry logic amplified traffic by 400%, overwhelming auth-service capacity.
Slower processing left thousands of Redis connections open simultaneously, starving the cache's event loop.
Cache contention prevented checkout-service from retrieving cart states, stalling the checkout flow.
Cache timeouts forced auth-service to fall back to database token lookups, instantly maxing out the DB connection pool.
Exhausted database connections prevented payments-service from recording transactional states, failing payments.
Exhausted database connections prevented inventory-service from reserving stock.

recoveryAction: Revert auth-service deployment to previous stable version (v2.4.0)

recoveryTimeline.event: Initiated rollback of auth-service deployment via CI/CD pipeline.
New pods running v2.4.0 begin passing health checks and accepting traffic.
v2.4.1 pods fully terminated. auth-service latency normalizes.
gateway-service retry storm subsides as requests succeed.
primary-db active connections drop from 100% to 25%.
